title: The Garden of the Ninefold Court
premise: Ines Okonkwo keeps the ledgers of the Ninefold Court's memory-guild, cataloguing stolen pasts she can never afford to buy back for herself. When prayers to the old gods begin landing in her ledger like unpaid debts, she discovers her own forgotten childhood was sold beneath the mountain — and that a client's soul is due for collection at the next dark moon. To save him, Ines must steal into the court itself, barter with the god who bought her memories, and choose between reclaiming her own past and freeing another's future. She walks out owning neither, but carrying something rarer: a name freely given.
about_author: Lena Almeida is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's letters before turning to fiction. She writes about debt, memory, and the small treasons of survival from a rain-dark coastal city.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Unpaid Prayers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Auditing the guild's books, Ines finds prayers addressed to dead gods appearing as entries — each one answered, each one signed in her own childhood handwriting. When a desperate client, Tomas, begs the guild to undo his soul-sale to the court beneath the mountain, the ledgers reveal his contract is valid and nearly due. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; Ines realizes the books know her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Owes
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with an interlude from the god Vessel-of-Salt. Descending through the market-tunnels, Ines trades stolen memories for passage and learns her own past was collateral in a bargain the guild's founder made generations ago. The god offers her a trade: her memories back for Tomas's soul. Emotional beat: temptation — the ache of belonging versus the guilt of purchase.

chapters.title: The Dark Moon Collection
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. On collection night, Ines attempts the theft of both contracts at once, forging entries in the ledger of the court itself. The forgery works until the god reads her handwriting and recognizes its author: the child who once wrote prayers here willingly. Betrayed by her own past self, Ines is caught between the god's claim and Tomas's screaming soul being drawn up through the mountain. Emotional beat: climax — identity as both weapon and trap.

chapters.title: A Name Freely Given
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Offered her full past in exchange for walking away, Ines instead tears out the founding page of the guild's oldest ledger, voiding every inherited debt — including her own. The court, bound by its own bookkeeping, must release Tomas. She surfaces with no memories restored but with Tomas alive, the guild remade, and a new name spoken aloud by someone who chose her. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution — belonging earned, not bought.
